import pandas as pd
from datetime import datetime

# Define the time range
start_time = datetime(2020, 5, 28, 3, 30)
end_time = datetime(2020, 5, 28, 4, 0)

# Load the metric files
node_metrics = pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_node.parquet')
container_metrics = pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_container.parquet')
service_metrics = pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_service.parquet')
middleware_metrics = pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_middleware.parquet')
app_metrics = pd.read_parquet('/telemetry/row/metric/metric_app.parquet')

# Combine all metrics into a single DataFrame
all_metrics = pd.concat([node_metrics, container_metrics, service_metrics, middleware_metrics, app_metrics])

# Convert the timestamp to UTC+8
all_metrics['timestamp'] = pd.to_datetime(all_metrics['timestamp']).dt.tz_localize('UTC').dt.tz_convert('Asia/Singapore')

# Filter metrics for the specified time range
filtered_metrics = all_metrics[(all_metrics['timestamp'] >= start_time) & (all_metrics['timestamp'] <= end_time)]

# Perform anomaly detection using the IQR method
Q1 = filtered_metrics['value'].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = filtered_metrics['value'].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
anomalies = filtered_metrics[(filtered_metrics['value'] < lower_bound) | (filtered_metrics['value'] > upper_bound)]

# Return the anomalies
anomalies
